verdicts.title: More on Diophantine sextuples
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
A rational Diophantine m-tuple is a set of m nonzero rationals such that the product of any two of them increased by 1 is a perfect square. The first rational Diophantine quadruple was found by Diophantus, while Euler proved that there are infinitely many rational Diophantine quintuples. In 1999, Gibbs found the first example of a rational Diophantine sextuple, and Dujella, Kazalicki, Mikic and Szikszai recently proved that there exist infinitely many rational Diophantine sextuples.

verdicts.title: Primes Solutions Of Linear Diophantine Equations
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Let k => 1, m => 1 be small fixed integers, gcd(k, m) = 1. This note develops some techniques for proving the existence of infinitely many primes solutions x = p, and y = q of the linear Diophantine equation y = mx + k.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns 'infinitely many primes solutions' of a linear Diophantine equation y = mx + k, which is a pure number theory result with no connection to Tseitin formulas or resolution proof width.

verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The paper deals with the resolution of third and fourth degree equations by means of radicals. It is a survey of some historical details about this fundamental problem.
